h1:
A 3-Day Nature Trip Around Chaiyaphum
Pa Hin Ngam, Sai Thong, Mo Hin Khao & Waterfalls
intro: Chaiyaphum does more with its sandstone hills than you'd expect — fields of oddly shaped rocks, cliffs that jut out over the valley, stone pillars as tall as buildings, and wide rock-shelf waterfalls you can actually swim in. This 3-day plan covers the full nature circuit — Pa Hin Ngam, Sai Thong, Mo Hin Khao, and Tat Ton — at a pace that won't wear you out.

blocks.html: Chaiyaphum's nature splits into two main zones. The western zone around Thep Sathit and Nong Bua Rawe districts holds Pa Hin Ngam and Sai Thong, both known for their rock fields and Siam tulip blooms. The zone closer to town is Mo Hin Khao and Tat Ton Waterfall. So this 3-day plan has you spending one night on the Thep Sathit side, then looping back to sleep in town for the second night — that way you're not driving long stretches back and forth every day.

blocks.text: The Chaiyaphum nature spots on this plan

items.name: Pa Hin Ngam National Park
items.blurb: The highlight is Lan Hin Ngam, a field of strangely shaped sandstone formations spread across the rock shelf, plus the Pha Sut Phaendin viewpoint looking out over the long Phang Hoei mountain range. In the rainy season there are pinkish-purple Siam tulip fields too. A shuttle tram runs from the headquarters up to the walking area.
items.price: Thai adults 40 THB, kids 20 THB + tram 30 THB

items.name: Sai Thong National Park
items.blurb: Just a short hop from Pa Hin Ngam. The standout is Pha Ham Hot, a rock ledge that sticks out over the cliff for shaky-legged photos, along with Sai Thong Waterfall flowing across a roughly 80-meter rock shelf down into the Wang Sai pool. There are several more Siam tulip fields up on the Phang Hoei ridge.
items.meta: Nong Bua Rawe district · Pha Ham Hot is a walk from the parking area
items.price: Park entry fee (check at the headquarters)

items.name: Mo Hin Khao (Phu Laen Kha National Park)
items.blurb: A cluster of large sandstone pillars standing in a grassy clearing, the tallest around 12 meters — which earned it the nickname Thailand's Stonehenge. You can walk a loop around them, with a trail continuing on to the million-year-old rock field and a sunrise viewpoint. It's much closer to town than the Thep Sathit side.
items.meta: Tha Hin Ngom, Mueang district · open roughly 07:00–18:00

items.name: Tat Ton National Park (Tat Ton Waterfall)
items.blurb: A waterfall about 6 meters high but a full 50 meters wide, with a long rock shelf up top that spreads the water out into a sheet. In the rainy season it runs full and you can swim at spots along it. It's only about 20 kilometers from town, making it a nice, easy way to close out the trip.
items.price: Thai adults 40 THB (seniors 60+ free), kids 20 THB

blocks.title: What to know about the Siam tulips first
blocks.html: The Siam tulip fields at Pa Hin Ngam and Sai Thong bloom only in the rainy season, roughly late June to mid-August — not year-round. Come at any other time and you'll see the rock fields and mountain views instead, which are still lovely, just without the pink flower fields. If you're timing your trip for the bloom, call the park headquarters first, because the timing shifts a little from year to year.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Into Thep Sathit, exploring Pa Hin Ngam

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Pa Hin Ngam + overnight on the Thep Sathit side

items.activity: Set off for Thep Sathit district
items.note: From Bangkok it's about 270 km to Pa Hin Ngam, a 4–5 hour drive. From Chaiyaphum town it's roughly 1.5–2 hours. You can stop for breakfast along the way.

items.activity: Arrive at Pa Hin Ngam National Park, pay the entry fee and board the tram
items.note: The tram takes you up to the walking area — easier on the legs than hiking up yourself.

items.activity: Walk the Lan Hin Ngam rock field with its odd sandstone shapes
items.note: There's a clear loop trail, an easy walk of about an hour. The midday sun is strong, so bring a hat and water.

items.activity: Lunch at the park restaurant, then on to the Pha Sut Phaendin viewpoint
items.note: Pha Sut Phaendin looks out over the long Phang Hoei range — it's the main photo spot at Pa Hin Ngam.

items.activity: If it's the rainy season, walk the Siam tulip fields inside the park
items.note: Outside flower season you can skip this and spend the time on the rock field and viewpoints instead.

items.activity: Check in to a place around Thep Sathit / Ban Rai and relax
items.note: This area has small resorts and park bungalows you can book. Staying nearby tonight means no long drive in the morning.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Sai Thong, Pha Ham Hot, then loop back to town

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Sai Thong + drive back to sleep in Chaiyaphum town

items.note: Heading out a bit early gets you soft light and cool air at Pha Ham Hot.

items.activity: Arrive at Sai Thong National Park and walk up to Pha Ham Hot (Sai Thong's edge-of-the-world cliff)
items.note: Pha Ham Hot is a rock ledge jutting about 1 meter off the cliff face — a hugely popular photo spot. People go up one at a time; watch your footing when it's rained.

items.activity: Walk down to Sai Thong Waterfall and the Wang Sai pool
items.note: The waterfall flows across a rock shelf around 80 meters wide. In the rainy season the water runs high and fast — you can swim at a few of the safer spots.

items.activity: Lunch, then if it's the rainy season swing by the Siam tulip fields on the Phang Hoei ridge
items.note: Sai Thong's tulip fields are about 10 km from the headquarters, spread across several meadows, blooming roughly late June to mid-August.

items.activity: Set off back to Chaiyaphum town
items.note: It's a fair distance, so allow 2–3 hours and take it easy — some of the mountain road is winding.

items.activity: Check in to your place in town, find dinner, take a short stroll
items.note: Sleeping in town tonight makes the final day, which is all close to town, much more convenient.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Mo Hin Khao, then wrapping up at Tat Ton

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Mo Hin Khao's Stonehenge + Tat Ton Waterfall

items.activity: Breakfast in town, then head out to Mo Hin Khao
items.note: Mo Hin Khao is in Tha Hin Ngom, Mueang district, about an hour's drive from town with a climb up the hill toward the end.

items.activity: Walk the Mo Hin Khao stone pillars
items.note: Large sandstone pillars stand in a grassy clearing, the tallest around 12 meters. You can walk a loop around them for photos.

items.activity: Continue on to the million-year-old rock field and viewpoint
items.note: There's a short forest trail beyond Mo Hin Khao — if you're up for it, walk on for more views; if it's hot, the main viewpoint is enough.

items.activity: Drive down the hill, have lunch, then head for Tat Ton Waterfall
items.note: Tat Ton is in Na Fai, about 20 km from town on an easy road.
The wide rock shelf up top spreads the water into a sheet. In the rainy season (June–September) it runs full and you can swim at spots along it — bring a change of clothes.

items.activity: Grab your final photos and head home
items.note: The park closes at 18:00, so leave with time to spare. If you're driving back to Bangkok, take it easy and break the trip up.

items: Your own car is the easiest option — Chaiyaphum's nature spots are spread out and hard to reach by public transport. If you don't drive, hire a car with a driver or charter one.
Mountain roads get slippery in the rainy season — especially the climbs up to Mo Hin Khao and Sai Thong. Drive slow, allow extra time, and avoid heavy downpours.
Sneakers or hiking shoes — the rock fields and some trail sections are uneven and slick when wet.
Hat, drinking water, sunscreen — the rock fields are wide open and the sun is strong from late morning through afternoon.
Cash — park entry and tram fees are cash only, and the mobile signal is patchy in spots up on the hills.

blocks.text: Adjusting the plan to the time you have

items.name: Only 1 day
items.blurb: Stick to the spots near town: Mo Hin Khao in the morning, then Tat Ton Waterfall in the afternoon — done in a single day without wearing yourself out.

items.name: 2 days, 1 night
items.blurb: Day one tackles Pa Hin Ngam and Sai Thong on the Thep Sathit side with one overnight; day two loops back and stops at Tat Ton before heading home.

items.name: Coming for the Siam tulips
items.blurb: Focus mainly on Pa Hin Ngam and Sai Thong, leaving plenty of time to walk the flower fields. Go early to beat the crowds and the strong sun.

faq.q: When do Chaiyaphum's Siam tulip fields bloom?
faq.a: They bloom only in the rainy season, roughly late June to mid-August each year, at both Pa Hin Ngam and Sai Thong. Outside that window there are no flower fields, but you can still visit the rock fields and viewpoints. If you're timing your trip for the bloom, call the park headquarters first, because the timing shifts a little from year to year.

faq.q: How many days do I need to see all of Chaiyaphum's nature?
faq.a: Three days and two nights is just right if you want to cover Pa Hin Ngam, Sai Thong, Mo Hin Khao, and Tat Ton — with one night on the Thep Sathit side and one in town. If you only have a single day, stick to the spots near town: Mo Hin Khao and Tat Ton.

faq.q: How much is park entry in Chaiyaphum?
faq.a: Pa Hin Ngam is 40 THB for Thai adults and 20 THB for kids, plus a 30 THB tram fee. Tat Ton is 40 THB for Thai adults, with seniors 60 and over free, and 20 THB for kids. Mo Hin Khao is around 30–50 THB. Actual fees can change, so double-check with the park headquarters.

faq.q: Can I do Chaiyaphum's nature spots without my own car?
faq.a: It's fairly tough, since the sights are inside parks that public transport doesn't reach. The better options are hiring a car with a driver, chartering one from town, or joining a tour with its own van — especially during the Siam tulip bloom.

faq.q: Can I do Mo Hin Khao and Tat Ton Waterfall on the same day?
faq.a: Easily, since both are close to Chaiyaphum town. Mo Hin Khao is in Tha Hin Ngom and Tat Ton is in Na Fai, about 20 km from town. I'd suggest Mo Hin Khao up on the hill in the morning, then dropping down to swim at Tat Ton in the afternoon.
